description: Open, versioned, adversarially-verified evidence base on containing authoritarianism and how societies change. Each entry is graded and carries a falsification trigger.

entries.title: Fascism is a form of political behavior, not a doctrine
Prebunking raises manipulation-resistance at scale
Prebunking does not reliably transfer to true/false discrimination
Intergroup contact correlates with reduced prejudice
Contact evidence has serious publication-bias/external-validity caveats
Status-threat vs economic-anxiety is unresolved
Operational openly-reproducible conflict early-warning systems exist
Committed minorities can tip systems; change cascades through networks
No universal critical-mass number; cascades are not automatic
The 'energy' driving cascades is complex contagion, not a mystical field
Refuted pseudoscience: 100th monkey, morphic resonance, consciousness fields
Reverse dominance hierarchy — evolutionary root of resisting tyranny (contested)
Self-governance avoids both tyranny and collapse — Ostrom (robust locally)
Peaceful societies exist / war not inevitable — antiquity contested
Cooperation is culturally evolved (framework robust; WEIRD mechanism contested)
RWA and SDO are robust, replicated individual-difference predictors of prejudice and anti-democratic attitudes
Milgram: the obedience EFFECT is robust/replicated; the 'blind obedience' INTERPRETATION is contested
Moral Foundations Theory: 5/6 innate universal foundations explaining the left-right divide
Mere categorization into arbitrary groups produces in-group favoritism in resource allocation (minimal group paradigm)
Asch conformity: a unanimous wrong majority makes a substantial minority conform to obvious errors
Blatant dehumanization (Ascent of Man) predicts hostile/exclusionary policy support beyond prejudice
'Dynamics of Contention' mechanism-process program: influential framework, contested as underspecified
Nonviolent campaigns succeeded ~2x as often as violent ones (53% vs 26%) in 1900-2006 NAVCO data
Social capital robustly correlates with governance, but causal direction and decline are contested
Repression backfire is real but conditional, not universal; net effect on mobilization is unresolved
US affective polarization is real, rising, and well-measured; its causal harm to democracy is contested
Megastudies cut partisan animosity, but that does not reliably lower anti-democratic attitudes
V-Dem and Freedom House measure a multi-decade global democratic recession; its global magnitude is contested
Anocracy + factionalism robustly forecasts instability, but the causal 'anocracy causes civil war' reading is partly a Polity coding artifact
Face-value survey estimates of US support for partisan violence are inflated by measurement error
Severe financial crises are systematically followed by far-right gains and political fragmentation
Income-democracy correlation is robust (Lipset); the causal claim income→democratization is contested
Inequality robustly correlates with democratic erosion risk, but causal direction and scope are contested
Oil/mineral wealth correlates robustly with authoritarianism; the unconditional causal 'curse' is contested
Import (China-shock) exposure raised far-right/populist voting in exposed regions — robust core, contested magnitude
YouTube algorithmic rabbit-hole radicalization is contested; extremist consumption is mostly demand-driven
Modern democratic backsliding is mostly gradual executive aggrandizement, not coups
Lateral reading is the expert strategy for evaluating online sources, and teaching it improves judgments
Institutions-prosperity correlation is robust (AJR); the causal claim inclusive institutions→long-run prosperity is contested
Conflict/backsliding forecasting has a real, peer-reviewed out-of-sample track record — but 'beats a no-change baseline' is metric- and task-dependent, not a settled fact
The 3.5% rule is a strong descriptive tendency, not a law — its own author documents the exceptions and warns against prescriptive use
